core.big_idea: Jesus was identified as God's Son and remained faithful under temptation.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Jesus' ministry: The Messiah Arrives within the Jesus, Gospel, and Discipleship cycle

claims.statement: At Jesus' baptism, the Spirit descends and a voice from heaven identifies Jesus as the beloved Son.
Jesus resists the tempter by answering from Scripture and refuses paths that would violate faithful allegiance to God.
Together the scenes present Jesus as God's Son who remains faithful under testing; Jesus' baptism should not be collapsed into a conversion template because the narrative purpose is different.

core.interpretation_skill: Locate on timeline; read immediate context; identify genre; separate observation and application

learning.foundation_objective: Explain from the passage that jesus was identified as god's son and remained faithful under temptation and locate the lesson on the whole-Bible timeline.
learning.extension_objective: Identify the immediate context and genre, then distinguish what the text directly states from a reasonable inference and application.
know: Jesus was identified as God's Son and remained faithful under temptation.
The lesson belongs in Jesus' ministry.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Mark one direct-text observation and one inference or application.
State the main point in context before applying it.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

Jesus resists the tempter by answering from Scripture and refuses paths that would violate faithful allegiance to God.
interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.
Read this as Gospel narrative / teaching and account for its immediate literary setting.
Distinguish explicit text, synthesis, inference, framework position, and prudential application.
theological_guardrails: Jesus' baptism is not a story for pressuring young people toward baptism. Distinguish Jesus' unique identity and mission from later conversion accounts.
Questions and disagreement may be expressed without embarrassment or coercion.

answer.text: Observe context and genre before concluding.
